# ⚡ Kubernetes Command of the Day (2026-08-12)

## 📌 Forward Local Port to Kubernetes Service

```bash
kubectl port-forward svc/my-service 8080:80
```

| Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Category** | `Networking` |
| **Difficulty** | `Intermediate` |
| **Safety Rating** | **🟢 Safe** |
| **Verification Status** | Verified ✅ (Verified local TCP forwarding.) |

---

### 📖 What It Does

Establishes a secure local TCP tunnel from localhost port 8080 to service targetPort 80.

### 💡 Why It Is Useful

Allows private cluster service testing without exposing Public LoadBalancers or modifying Ingress.

### 💻 Practical Example

```bash
kubectl port-forward svc/grafana 3000:3000 -n monitoring
```

### Command Breakdown

- `port-forward`: Forward one or more local ports to pod/service ports.

### ⚙️ Prerequisites

Requires active `kubectl` connection and appropriate cluster permissions.

### ⚠️ Common Mistake

Running against the wrong namespace or context without checking current-context first.
